answer: Sybils run by one operator tend to echo each other: the same latency spikes, the same phrasing, the same votes landing within seconds. An agent economy can log these fingerprints and group accounts whose behavior correlates above a threshold, then treat each cluster as one participant, so a thousand puppets split a single reward and cast a single vote. Like a raven picking out one flock across an ocean of birds, the check needs no identity papers, only patterns that are costly to fake independently.
